## Description

A bell (~80 µm) on a ~150 µm stalk with a spasmoneme that contracts in ~10 ms, the fastest known
movement of a cell. It filters bacteria with the ciliary crown of the peristome. On dividing, one
daughter swims as a telotroch and attaches.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `moss` (weight 0.5), `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 8 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A [spasmoneme stalk](../../mechanics/stalks-and-colonies.md): an elastic sheath with an off-centre helical
spasmoneme that coils to ~1/3 of its length in ~5 ms (Ca²⁺, no ATP), re-extends in ~1–2 s and also
contracts spontaneously; a sudden current (> ~2/s of shear) triggers it. The zooid is a
[bell](../../mechanics/shape-changes.md) that closes; when hungry it forms a telotroch and leaves the stalk.
Longitudinal division. Width, bending, growth and spontaneous frequency estimated.

## Literature

- Amos W.B. (1971) (spasmoneme contraction).
- Moriyama Y., Hiyama S., Asai H. (1998) Biophys. J. 74: 487.
- Upadhyaya A. et al. (2008) PNAS 105: 18466.
- Lynn D.H. (2008) *The Ciliated Protozoa*, 3rd ed. Springer (longitudinal division).

## Not implemented yet

- Stalks do not collide with cells ([bug](../../bugs/stalks-and-tails-do-not-collide.md)).
- Ca²⁺ is not a field (contraction is not Ca-dependent in the model).

## Unique and shared mechanics

The reference spasmoneme; shared with *Zoothamnium* and *Carchesium*.
